newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coffee roasters face supply problems -union.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee roasters face supply problems -union.

text.p: Brazilian coffee roasters are now experiencing problems obtaining green coffee for roasting in the domestic market, according to an indicator drawn up by the Sao Paulo State Coffee Industry Union.
The indicator works on a basis of one to 9, with nine representing the tightest supply.
For the period May 26-30, the indicator rose to 5.42 points, moving into what is considered to be a critical area.
For the previous period, the indicator reached 4.88 points, suggesting selective supply.

"In our sector, not just one, but many industries will close their doors if this scenario of a coffee shortage and high prices continues over the coming months," union president Nathan Herszkowicz said in a statement.
For Herszkowicz the solution lies in increased supply from government coffee stocks.
"The CDPC (coffee council)...needs to decide urgently a revision of auction policy - quantity, program and prices - in such a way as to bring order to the domestic market," he said.
High raw material prices have forced roasters to adjust their wholesale prices to an average of between 5.90 to 6.10 reais ($5.51 to $5.70) per kg, Herszkowicz said.
This means shoppers will see shelf prices of around seven reais ($6.54) per kg. This is still cheaper however than at the start of the government's anti-inflation plan which began in July 1994.
"While our current worry is about lack of supply, we are afraid that a continuation of the present situation will lead us to even higher prices, with a subsequent drop in demand," Herszkowicz said.
